svg.text: Automated Crack Detection in SEM/TXM Micrographs
Full workflow: detection → manual correction → machine learning, worked example: 260708_316_H_b2_front_CBS_002

text.tspan: Every candidate across all 2 page(s) (295 total, 112 kept), bordered red = kept / cyan =
rejected -- used to spot-check and hand-correct labels for the next training round.

svg.text: Read-only w.r.t. the base pipeline above (F) -- lets a human correct what it missed, then retrains on those corrections
newly labeled corrections retrain (H) for the next round

text.tspan: Figure 1. Automated crack-detection pipeline for SEM/TXM micrographs of annealed stainless steel, plus its manual-correction and retraining loop. Raw 16-bit
micrographs are contrast-stretched and auto-cropped (A), background-flattened (B), and segmented into candidate dark regions (C). A Frangi vesselness filter
and connected-component analysis extract an 8-feature vector per candidate (D), which a logistic-regression classifier separates into cracks and artifacts;
a minimum-spanning-tree bridges fragments of the same physical crack (E), producing a binary mask, numbered overlay, and measurements (F). Read-only against
that result, a human can then directly add, correct, or erase regions in a browser paint app using the same red=crack/cyan=artifact convention as (F) plus a
magenta eraser -- two touching red regions are always merged into one crack -- or work through review sheets of harder candidates (notches along a crack's
own boundary, corridors between bridged fragments, or the wider gradient-fade interior a flattening filter can suppress) that the base mask's brightness
threshold missed (G). Those labels train a small classifier, calibrated with an extra distance/brightness rule for the hardest candidate type and validated
by leave-one-out testing against every known negative rather than trusted on cross-validation alone; accepted regions are folded into the crack mask, and
the freshly labeled corrections retrain the loop for the next round (H). Worked example shown: 260708_316_H_b2_front_CBS_002.
